sections.title: Molecular profile of mucinous carcinoma
sections.intro: MOC is a **KRAS / CDKN2A-initiated, copy-number-progressing** carcinoma that develops through benign and borderline precursors. It is genetically distinct from colorectal, appendiceal and gastric mucinous tumours, and closest to pancreatic adenocarcinoma, from which ERBB2 amplification and RNF43 mutation separate it [7]. The only treatment-selecting biomarker enriched in MOC is **HER2**. **Pathology in brief:** after revised diagnostic criteria, primary MOC fell to about 3–5% of epithelial ovarian cancers [1,7]. Bilaterality, small tumour size, surface involvement, a nodular pattern, infiltrative invasion, hilar or vascular invasion and signet ring cells favour metastasis. A unilateral large tumour with expansile invasion and benign or borderline areas favours an ovarian primary. Immunohistochemistry (CK7, CK20, CEA, CA19.9, CDX2, SATB2, PAX8 and others) assists but is often of limited value, because most primary MOC show intestinal differentiation [1]. **Expansile vs infiltrative invasion matters for stage I prognosis.** Lethal recurrences occurred mainly in infiltrative tumours (recurrence 3/29 expansile vs 6/35 infiltrative) [8], and in a Dutch population cohort stage I expansile tumours had fewer recurrences (5% vs 14%) and better overall and recurrence-free survival [9].

notes.title: Practical consequence for testing
notes.md:
1. **Confirm the primary before choosing systemic therapy.** In both randomized first-line datasets with central review, most "mucinous ovarian" cases were reinterpreted as metastatic [1,6].
2. **HER2 IHC (with ISH for 2+) is the one biomarker that changes options** in advanced or recurrent MOC, and it is enriched here (18.8–26%) compared with HGSC (4.6%) [11,21]. Heterogeneity is common, so test the recurrence if the archival block is negative [10,12].
3. **BRCA/HRD, FRα and PD-L1 do not open a trial-proven option in MOC**: the pivotal PARPi, mirvetuximab and pembrolizumab trials did not enrol mucinous carcinoma.
4. **MMR testing is very low-yield** (0/34 and 0/20) [11,13]. A MMRd "mucinous" tumour should prompt review for an endometrioid, mixed or extra-ovarian primary.

notes.title: Reading Table 1
notes.md:
- **No randomized trial has tested adjuvant chemotherapy in MOC.** The RCT evidence is a pooled all-histology result in which mucinous was 20%, with a death count favouring chemotherapy (10/90 vs 22/90) but no mucinous HR and no histology interaction (P=.55) [2]. These trials predate the primary vs metastatic review standard, and the invasion pattern was not reported.
- **Registry data do not show a survival benefit for stage I MOC** (NCDB stage I adjusted HR 1.18; stage IC IPTW HR 0.88; SEER validation HRs >1) [29,30]. These are uncontrolled and cannot separate expansile from infiltrative tumours.
- **The expansile/infiltrative split changes the prior risk, not the proven effect of chemotherapy.** Recurrences in stage I are about 5% (expansile) vs 14% (infiltrative) [9], and lethal recurrences were mainly infiltrative [8]. No source here compares chemotherapy vs observation within infiltrative stage I.
- **More cycles did not help mucinous tumours in GOG-157** (6 vs 3 cycles recurrence HR 1.68, 0.30–9.29, 31 patients) [27].

notes.title: Traps in Table 2
notes.md:
1. **GOG-0241 is the only MOC randomized trial and it is uninformative for decision-making**: 50 of 330 patients, all CIs wide, and only 45% of reviewed cases were primary MOC [1]. The confirmed-MOC OS HR of 0.36 for oxaliplatin–capecitabine (p=0.14) rests on 18 patients.
2. **Poor platinum–taxane response in "advanced MOC" is consistent across series** (ORR 26.3% vs 64.9% [33]; 38.5% vs 70% [34]; worse PFS and OS in pooled RCT data, PFS HR 2.10 and OS HR 2.66 vs serous [4]). But central pathology review was uneven in the older cohorts (Hess used in-house pathology re-review; SOCRATES had none), and in the GOG five-arm trial most "mucinous" cases were probably metastatic, with the same poor OS as reviewed primaries [6].
3. **The GI-type regimen signal is retrospective and confounded** (bevacizumab 50% vs 4%; 59% stage I; univariable HR) [32]. It supports discussing GI-type chemotherapy, not a claim of superiority.
4. **Dose-dense weekly paclitaxel gave no signal in clear cell/mucinous** (PFS HR 1.03–1.06) [5,36].
5. **No PARPi or immunotherapy maintenance trial enrolled MOC**; trial-wide HRs in OVCA_HGSC_Algorithm_v1.2 Table 2B do not apply.

notes.title: GOG-0241 dosing vs NTUH templates
notes.md:
- **Oxaliplatin–capecitabine (GOG-0241): oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² D1 + capecitabine 850 mg/m² PO BID D1–14, q3w ×6** [1]. **There is no NTUH capecitabine template.** The NTUH oxaliplatin–fluoropyrimidine options are infusional: OV biweekly mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 400 mg/m² + 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus + 2400 mg/m² over 46 h, D1 and D15 of a 28-day course, 6 courses) and OV biweekly mFOLFOX4(4天3夜)(豪哥) (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² + leucovorin 200 mg/m² D1; 5-FU 400 mg/m² bolus + 2400 mg/m² over 22 h listed on D1 and D2; 14-day cycle, 12 courses). In Kurnit's GI-type group, 6/26 received 5-FU + oxaliplatin and 17/26 capecitabine + oxaliplatin; doses were not reported [32].
- **Carboplatin–paclitaxel (GOG-0241): carboplatin AUC 5/6 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w; bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w** [1]. OV Paclitaxel and Carboplatin uses AUC 5 + 175 mg/m²; OV Paclitaxel and Carboplatin with Avastin leaves the bevacizumab mg/kg field blank.
- OV Paclitaxel and Oxaliplatin (175 + 100 mg/m² q3w), OV Docetaxel (75) + Oxaliplatin (100) and OV P-HDFL (Carboplatin (5) + 5-FU (2600)) (carboplatin AUC 5 + 5-FU 2600 mg/m² over 24 h + leucovorin 300 mg/m², 21-day course) exist, but none of these combinations was a tested regimen in the MOC-specific sources above.

sections.title: 3. Recurrent disease
sections.intro: Table 3 keeps the platinum-sensitivity split. **3A** = relapse ≥6 months after last platinum; **3B** = relapse <6 months, plus HER2-directed and checkpoint-inhibitor rows whose MOC data do not report a platinum-free interval.

notes.title: Why this split is thin in MOC
notes.md: Only one MOC-specific recurrence series reports the platinum-free interval (SOCRATES, >6 months) [47]. HER2-directed evidence in MOC is case-level and not stratified by platinum sensitivity, so it sits in 3B. Most modern platinum-resistant trials (MIRASOL, ROSELLA, KEYNOTE-B96, KEYNOTE-100, NRG-GY003) did not enrol mucinous carcinoma. Median post-relapse survival in a 151-patient MOC cohort was 5.0 months [31].

notes.title: Reading notes for Table 3
notes.md:
- **Recurrent MOC responds poorly even when platinum-sensitive**: ORR 36.4% vs 62.6% and OS from recurrence 17.9 vs 28.8 months in SOCRATES, from 11 evaluable mucinous patients [47].
- **HER2 is the only targeted lead with MOC-level evidence**, and that evidence is anecdotal (one response in three trastuzumab cases [12]; one T-DXd partial response [57]). DESTINY-PanTumor02 supports T-DXd for HER2 IHC 3+ ovarian cancer of any histotype, but did not report histotype [20]. Given HER2 3+ in 18.8–26% of MOC [11,21], this is the practical reason to test HER2.
- **Checkpoint inhibitors, mirvetuximab, relacorilant and PARPi** have no MOC-specific data. MOC is FRα-negative (0/117) and MMR-proficient in the series held [13,16], and 86% immune-cold [18].
